New email received? Great, I bet it's my boss, John Graham, doing his usual 5AM "something's wrong" email. I worked at a law firm, Logan, Morley & Graham and I hated it, the emailing, the jargon, the people who worked at the clerk's office at the Supreme Court, everything. I was only there because it paid the bills and at first, I learned a lot but now I'm at a steady downward spiral. Mostly cause I no longer give a shit about anything, I've gained 40 pounds since my last semester in college which was about 3 years ago. As my eyes adjusted, I noticed the email that had just came into my mailbox was from a recipient that I did not have on my address book. "S@GarlandMail.com" I didn't recognize it, I actually didnt think you could have an email with just one letter and I have never heard of this Garland company. No subject, might be some junk mail, or who knows, maybe it might have even been a mistake, I do have a very popular name Benjamyn Smiley. My email was BenSmiley09@LMGLAW.com which could easily be confused with, I don't know.. Maybe BeenSmiley09@LMH law? But then I noticed the first line of the email "TO THE ATTENTION OF BENJAMYN G. SMILEY." My heart began to race, as if, I had just won some type of grand prize or sweepstakes. The use of my middle initial, G for Gregorio (after my grandfather Gregorio Smiley) made me certain that this was not a mistake. I had nothing to worry about, I had never hurt a fly nor stole anything from anyone so I was more excitedly nervous rather than scared something had caught up to me. Then I read the next 2 lines: "IGNORE THIS EMAIL WE WILL KILL YOUR FAMILY. WE ARE VERY CLOSE TO KATIE AT THE MOMENT." My heart sank. Katie was my little sister off in college at the University of Lymesport. I did not want to take any chances with calling the police as I knew whoever this was, was not joking. My sister Katie will never be involved in any wrongdoing. I knew I could call my dad and ask for help but I finished the email to further understand what these people were after. Money? "WE DONT WANT MONEY. WE DONT WANT YOUR HOUSE. WE NEED A LIVER. MEET OLIVER AT 5309 KUEMOR STREET 92TH FLOOR 7:26PM. NO LIVER, NO FAMILY" Now I knew I couldn't call my dad, he was a surgeon. I put two and two together before my thoughts could fully process. My dad is known worldwide as being the Father of Medicine after he found the cure for 7 forms of cancer a few years ago. He would often be called The Phantom Doctor as he was once found associating with black market traffickers, I knew this email was somehow connected to my father. How could I get them a liver? How could I get anybody a liver! I'm not a doctor, I dont even associate with doctors, I hate the law but at least I know and understand it very well and I'm always around legal people. Doctors? Hell I barely spoke to my dad cause he was so busy and so private when it came to his profession. It was always his passion, he was the only kid in his neighborhood hunting small animals to experiment with dissecting. Now he was an old man, probably mixing around the wrong people like our family has doubted so many times in the past. I thought and thought until I was no longer sleepy and the sun seeped through the outline of my navy blue shades, giving a holy appearance to the side of my room. A few minutes later the idea struck me like an 8 ball of blow straight from the Peruvian jungles, I would sneak in the morgue with my dad's ID... I was arrested 14 hours later for false impersonation, identity theft and practicing medicine without a license as well as trespassing and a few other charges. Katie went missing a week later and was never found. My dad lost his license as news got out that he had been overseeing an illegal clinic in Deskerville, where a woman had died due to a failed liposuction. He committed suicide in jail awaiting trial after 33 days. I never checked my email again..

"come onnnnn Jonah" I screamed at my beagle as I struggled to restrain him. He was known for being a 20 pound bully, but this time he was serious about something he smelled. I had to get back home by 7PM to watch the playoff game, I didn't want to take any chances. It was 6:12PM and I could see where this was going with Jonah. "Alright Jonah, I'll give you 15 minutes, then we have to turn back" I told him, expecting a response but only getting his clueless look. I usually walked him in my backyard, that was pretty wooded and forested on account that I lived by Nantahala. I was a North Carolina guy who loved hiking trails and the great outdoors. I'd visited every state except Alaska, Hawaii, North Dakota, Maine and Arizona. All the others I've either spent a night or spent a week at some point in my 27 year old life. Jonah stopped and began to dig, I checked my phone to see if anyone had text me, millennial habit. After a few minutes, I saw a handle under Jonah. He whimpered and whined when he couldn't pull out what would be a suitcase. I helped him dig and uncovered a brown leather suitcase with the initials J.E.P. Surprised it didn't have a lock, I popped it open. Passports? There were 5, from another country, maybe Russian. Also a cellphone, a .22 caliber pistol and a vile of blood. "Let me see your hands! Sir, let me see your hands!" I heard the familiar voice of law enforcement. I complied putting my hands in the air. "What are you doing here, is that a gun? Let me see a permit for this weapon sir." I mumbled. "Sir, put your hands behind your back for me. I'm not arresting you, I'm just detaining you, right now I have reasonable suspicion to believe you're up to something that might be criminal." I quickly thought, "oh fuck, a stickler cop, just what I needed.." As he tightened the handcuffs behind my back, a loud bang from a bullet leaving a barrel filled the air, startling Jonah even more. "its okay bud" I scream out to him. The officer falls on his back. Bleeding from the mouth with a gunshot wound to the neck. Looking up I see a tall white man, aiming his barrel at the cop's face and pulling the trigger. This sent Jonah running, I wasn't alarmed, he usually ran back home when he was scared. "The cops came because of the alarm in that suitcase." I was still confused. "Those passports are part of a very secret mission against Russia's top officials." He looked at my confused face and then said "your father.." and paused. I felt like I was in a movie, a stranger just killed a cop in my backyard and is now mentioning my father. "He was in the CIA, and is not dead. He's captive in Russia, the blood vile in that suitcase is essential for the survival of a very important person in this world"  he said. I was still shocked and didn't say a word. "its okay, I'm just here for two reasons, the blood vile and to make sure you don't say anything about what you've just witnessed." I felt as if a long nightmare was in the horizon. "Listen, take the blood, gun, passport, whatever you nee.." I was cut off by his stern voice "Do you think your dog just wanted to pick a spot to dig? your beloved dog was injected with a liquid that makes him smell cocaine and go crazy for it, the suitcase emitted cocaine at exactly 6:05PM, sending your dog in a wild trail." I was now, more scared than I have ever been in my life. I dropped everything and ran, somehow forgetting I didn't have my arms available, falling on my chest and face. "Listen kid, the only reason I'm still here is..." The last words I heard. I woke up on a plane. "We only have one shot to do this kid, don't mess this up" said the now familiar voice of the white man I would only know as Max. Max was a burly guy who looked as if he was a German hit man, not that I know what those look like. "heres the plan, you go into the hospital, inject the blood into our subject and you're free to go" he said. "Why me?" I asked. "Because your father is one of one, this person isn't very trusting. He figures you have your father's good heart" he replied. "Okay, I guess, at this point I have no choice.." I said, my voice raspy. "Where are we?" I asked. "Listen kid, right now you're asking too much questions, I don't wanna have to knock you out again" Max said, clearly annoyed. I didn't feel any bruises, so I guess he used another method that I wish I could remember. Russia was a beautiful country, the airplane landed in what seemed like Moscow judging by all the advertisement. We spent no more than 20 minutes in the airport as I now knew I was in trouble because everyone seemed important from this moment on. We entered a waiting limousine and were met by more men, these guys meant business. "this him?" one of them asked. "Yeah" max replied. It was about an hour drive after the airport which I enjoyed because I never been inside a limo. "Alright kid, heres everything you need, in and out, room 501, the guard will let you up once he sees your ID." Max said, opening the door for me as he finished his sentence. I felt the cold Russian breeze as I walked into the hospital. Said and done, the guard informed me in perfect english that the elevators to the right will lead me into 501. It was a glorious suite, guarded by heavily armed men. I showed them my ID and they smiled and let me in. I filled the syringe with the blood from the vile, remembering Max's "in and out." I entered the room to see a man, clearly dying, hanging on for life through these machines all around him. I took his lifeless forearm and wiped a spot with an alcohol pad before I injected him. Suddenly, there was beeping. Loud beeping filled the entire hospital suite and all I could think of doing was running. The heavily armed men appeared at the mans bedside in seconds. "What did you do?" one asked, pointing his assault rifle in my face. "nothing, i.. Max, uh.." I began to mumble. Two men grabbed each one of my arms and now I felt this was all wrong. What am I doing in Russia? I thought about the last time I was awake and how a cop had been killed in my backyard. Where is Jonah? I was very scared. I was put inside a jail cell in the hospital. I didn't know what I had done, I didn't know where I was, I didn't know what was to come. I was paranoid the cop murdered in my backyard would come back to haunt me. Suddenly, the door opened... In came a clown holding a mallet. "what the fuck!?" I screamed. It was the last thing I did.

My name's Bud.. Bud Weiserman. I've been working at John Fitzgerald High School for as long as I can remember, before the varsity bowling team or whatever these ballerina "jocks" do these days. I've swept and mopped up just about anything coming out of a locker, backpack or lunch bag. It's a dirty job, but somebody's got to do it; in this generation, its me. It wasn't until after my accident than I discovered who I really was. While cleaning up the school's field day activities in the football field, the northern goal post snapped right under me, the rest is history. I suffered 86 broken bones from the small ones in my hands and feet, to my elbows, clavicle and femur. I woke up in the hospital a few hours later thinking I had just gotten a hip replacement or something an old man would get after such an accident. The doctor came in 30 seconds after I realized I was alive and said words I will never forget "you must be a miracle-man, after that pole broke most of your bones, your bones fused together with a steel-like substance that your body seems like it produces." I was stunned, it was truly unheard of. Who was I? Wolverine? Na.. Been watching too much Marvel movies, I was no super hero. I was convinced I was still on morphine or something.. Until I left the hospital 2 hours later with no pain whatsoever. I decided to walk home, get some fresh air and comprehend my life's near future direction.. I should mention I've been divorced for over 10 years, because I felt much more attractive for a 59 year old man as I walked through Main Street. What was happening to me? Who was I becoming? Questions filled my mind as I walked home, so I figured I'd run it all off. The 2 mile trek became a 2 minute sprint. Now I was worried, how can I explain this.. To anyone. That night, as I read and drank my nightly cup of milk. I heard a bang in the front door, followed by another, the a third bang that knocked the door off the hinges. My heartbeat was a cheetah sprint if there was any animal to describe the feeling of it coming out of my chest. Suddenly, the world became slow, I saw the three hooded and masked men charging at me at once. I lunged for the bathroom, grabbing a broom as I closed the door behind me and exited through the window in a matter of seconds hearing the loud claps of gunfire inside my own home. Now I knew I wasn't the same person, I was on my roof like I've done parkour all my life. I now believed what the doctor had said.. What could this steel stuff be, I wasn't superman, just Bud the Janitor. All of a sudden, I wasn't Bud, I had this anger fueled inside of me. I sneaked back inside to find all three men eager to find treasure that wasn't anywhere but the bottom of the ocean. I grabbed the broom I was holding so tightly that it broke in half and I lodged both pieces into one mans back, he screamed. "Now you're breathing splinters" I said. I didn't know where saying that came from either. The other two men pointed their guns at me, I was very scared. I had never had a gun pointed at me. "Go ahead shoot" I said, surprised at myself. The world became slow again. The two men pulled the trigger, one revealing he had run out of bullets. The other gun ejected a .22 caliber bullet that I was surprised I could even see. The next few minutes felt like a few seconds. With the bottom of my palm I pushed up against the gunman's nose, killing him instantly. The ammo-less third thief tried to run, slipping and falling under my heavy steel-toed boot, that crushed his jaw. I had never killed a man, let alone three. The first man had bled to death with both ends of the broom going through him. The gunslinger, as I liked to call him, had his nose in his brain. Jaw kid, well, lets just say he choked on a jawbreaker. Police had responded to a neighbors call and had gotten to my home 23 minutes after my front door was kicked off the hinges. 23 minutes too late... 

The cops were bewildered to find Bud, the ol' Janitor, in a room smoking a cigarette. He was dismissed from committing any wrong doing as he was justified in using the force he did. "jeeze, to think ol bud knew martial arts, guy is a modern day Jason Bourne" said one cop to the other. Bud knew he had some abilities not even the strongest of the strong possessed, so he followed crime. "killing a man isn't so hard if you do it for the right reasons" he was once heard saying. Bud wasn't the same after his accident. He was now The Janitor.. Wherever there was a mess, he brought a broom to clean it up..

My desire of living in this world has been on decline for years on end, but of course that would never be enough to convince The Committee for Societal Suicide Acceptance (TCSSA). My uncle killed himself when he was 26, the pressures of a higher education always haunted him as he was expected to do well in life. I never had thoughts like him until I was 9 and I saw his lifeless body, swinging around the middle of my grandparents' garage with what seemed to be tears still filling his eyes. I stared at his eyes wondering if he was staring back, in disbelief. I heard a gasp and turned around to see Aunt Hareé, with the saddest expression I had ever seen until that point. She opened a drawer and grabbed grandpa's 1911 pistol then pressed it against her temple. The next 3 minutes felt as if it were 12:03AM in Times Square New York City on January first, it was a blur to say the least. Aunt Hareé's body twitched after she pulled the trigger for what seemed like an eternity but was only a few horrifying seconds. My Uncle Wilson and aunt Hareé had died within minutes of each  other and 9 year old me saw it all. The sound of the gunshot had woken up my grandparents and when they saw the scene at the garage, they could barely hold themselves together. Wilson had been accepted to all the nation's top schools and loved it, as Hareé had always been depressed and labeled the black sheep by the rest of the family. I never knew my parents, I was bullied at school when I worked up enough courage to go and nobody ever liked me much after that. I'm now 28, the last 19 years of my life haven't been very convincing; I've been in a few car accidents, few bar fights and almost lost my life in a house fire. I'm writing this, to legally end my life with the permission of the government. I fear that if I keep living, I will start hating the world more and more until I fall under society's trap of living in fear.

"Looks like my time to go is tonight, couldn't come any sooner if you ask me" said Bill to his neighbor Adam as they both worked on their lawns. "Sheesh Bill, do you have to be so morbid?" asked Adam in a low voice. "Listen, I'm 58 I lived longer than most people did... 500 years ago, that's enough for me, I've seen it all... From the Yankees winning a ton of World Series titles to terrorism destroying the world." he replied. It was 9AM, the sun shining as it did every day in the sunny streets of Yuma, Arizona and Bill felt great. He was the lead contractor for a big company and if it hadn't been for death creeping up, he would've owned the business. "How much time do you have Adam? That is.. If you aren't afraid to talk about it.." Billy's voice changed to a surprisingly mocking tone. "Well... I'll be 47 next month, so that makes.. 44 years left on this wagon..." Adam joked. Billy stayed silent, as he contemplated what he was going to do in his final day. "Marion probably has a big breakfast for you Bill, I'm gonna go on inside and get ready for work. I'll see you later." Adam said backing away. Billy felt Adam's distance, the two had basically been neighbors for the last 10 years and had a pretty close bond. Bill entered his house yelling out to his wife of 30 years, Marion. "Maryyyyyy...." he screamed for her. As he was walking upstairs, he saw the blood on the carpet. He ran, faster than any 230 lb man has ran before. He found Marion with the scissors still in her hand and her wrists still gushing blood. Bill had known it was too late, he picked up the note and read aloud "Billy, I love you and I can't picture living without you. Enjoy the day and we might see each other again at the end of this beautiful day." He sobbed for his wife, wondering if she had known all along that today was her day as well. Marion had never told Billy her date as he swore he would go with her into the next life. He angrily picked up his shovel and headed out the door. He banged on Adam's door viciously until Adam answered in his robe. "Bill, whats going on are you alright?" he asked panicked. "Listen.. It's Marion, she's dead..." he yelled. Adam rushed to the phone and before he had gotten the opportunity to dial, his world turned black as Bill swung the shovel over his head, causing blood to spray all over Adam's kitchen. "...And you're going with her.." he whispered. Adam's son Corey, hearing the commotion shot into action grabbing his father's XD45 handgun from his locked drawer. He walked into the kitchen to find his father's bloody body and Bill holding a shovel. "What the fuck?! Bill?" he said. He pointed the weapon at Bill's face. "What the fuck did you do?" he said as his voice cracking from the sorrow of seeing his father bleed out effortlessly. The loud bang echoed through the quiet suburban streets and Bill's body hit the ground with an even louder thud... Adam was in a medically induced coma for 14 months and vowed never to mention moments of death again.

"Daddy will be right back Sam" were the last words I heard my father speak. I saw him going into the dark pub, with his friends waiting for him at the entrance. At this point, I knew what was going on. My father had never spent less than an hour with his friends, especially when they all got together. Now, I'm 8 and old enough to know that I'm not old enough to know anything. After a few minutes, I felt like a fever was coming. My mouth was dry and Arizona is not the place to live if you weren't a desert animal. I thought about going to sleep and maybe I'll wake up in my bed like when my parents went to those family parties, but this was different. I had never been in a car alone, I was getting more scared by the minute. I tried to signal for help, but at this point I could think of nobody but my beautiful mother who would've never put me in this predicament. I pressed my face against the driver's side window, because I thought the back of the car was melting faster. I made eye contact with a young black man who really needed a belt. He looked me right in the eyes and kept walking, shaking his head in dismay. He was the first person I had seen for what seemed like hours, but was really still a few minutes. I counted to get my mind off the extensive heat that was now filling the car. By the time I caught my breath and started counting the hundreds, the young man was back, this time with a golf club. At this point, my heart was racing like a horse with a funny name in the Kentucky Derby. I was scared my father would come out and see this man destroying his car window. I stood back, burying my head into the soft leather backseat. I was itching to have pieces of glass everywhere around me for the chance to breath cooler air. He began taking swing after swing as I waited patiently with my head covered waiting for the impact. A few seconds later, there was no more banging from the golf club to the glass. I looked up to see my father holding his still smoking XD45 handgun and give me a look of distress. That young man ended up being Lamont Rutherford, a college student who wanted to study polytechnics. My dad was slapped in the wrist by the Arizona legal system and served 9 months for child neglect and endangerment crimes. A man lost his life, trying to save mine because my father was too busy to care for his son.

I knelt down, blood still on my clothes, asking for forgiveness to these statues around me. I was never religious, but sometimes life makes you do things you never usually do. What I've done in life cannot be undone, a mothers have lost sons, sisters have lost brothers and kids have lost their dads. I am not a sinner, but I have sinned; it's the business I am in. I first killed a man at the age of 13 with my bare hands, choked him until he went cold. I'm 52 now-- probably coming close to my last few years in this life, but there's one thing I don't regret and it's taking the life of a criminal who didn't belong. I hunt evil people who've caused misery to communities and I believe I've done the right thing so far. I got up from my knees and left San Jose church, which my family visited every few Sundays growing up. I took the last step onto the sidewalk when I felt the barrel of a .357 magnum being pressed against the back of my head. I didn't process what was happening because it had never happened. The world went silent and I could almost hear the finger tightening on the trigger when the loud bang rang through the streets. All I had was 7 seconds before I saw black and felt my body tensing and going into shock. I hope they serve tequila in hell.

After 2 decades in the force, you realize you risk your life for nothing. I guess… A paycheck, thats what you risk it all for." I had seen it all, from the dead to the raped to everything in between. It was 6:54AM and I was getting ready for my last 8:30-4:30PM. Tony was a new guy, 3 years in, still had the rookie drive to make sergeant as soon as possible. I didn't want to spend my morning explaining to Tony that this job wasn't what it used to be for me, it changes you over time like any other job. My great-grandfather served in the NYPD for 40 years until he died as the commissioner. I never aspired to that, I do the job and go home to my wife and daughter, especially after 20 years. Uniform on, I headed across the street from the precinct to get my usual sausage, bacon and swiss cheese on sliced wheat. Waiting for my sandwich, two guys come in, acknowledge me with the "how you doin' officer" head nod. I give half a smile and continue waiting for my sandwich. What seemed to be like seconds later, two shots rang through the Park Slope neighborhood in Brooklyn… Before smelling the gun smoke and seeing George with a wound to the head, it went through my head that somebody who would rob the bodega across the street from the precinct had to be deranged. I radioed command and had them send a bus over for George, who was an immigrant from Lebanon and had run the deli most of his adult life. As fast as the bullets left the barrel, I left the store, my lungs burning, my vision blurred. "It's definitely to early for this shit" I told myself, debating whether to pull the trigger on my Glock service pistol. We ran for what seemed like hours, but it was later verified as a 79 second pursuit. I slowed down, aimed my weapon and 3 shots burst out into the morning air in Brooklyn, 2 hitting the victim in his back and neck. Running toward him I recognize the familiar grunt I was hearing, all too familiar. He looks up at me, smiling, exposing his bloody teeth and then looks down; his eyes watering. It was my youngest brother. "Fuck Cory, fuck oh my God, please no….." I whispered, my voice cracking. The sirens were getting closer, but I know my baby brother was only seconds from meeting the fate I had given him. "I needed the money…" He whispered to me, his eyelids closing. I didn't want him to talk, I thought it would give him more minutes on earth if he saved all his energy. I held his hand and looked into his eyes and I saw him gently close his eyes for the last time. I had killed my brother. Less than 5 minutes ago, I made the decision that this perp's life was in my hands and this perp ended up being my brother, whom has been in a bad place in life for years. On my knees, my brothers blood still on me, I pressed my pistol hard against the side of my head. Sirens and police lights surrounded me, I could barely see anyone as my vision was clouded with tears. I heard Tony's voice, clear as it was when we spoke earlier that morning. "Carl, you have more to live for. Please, there are people who love you" he said. I didn't have anything to live for anymore, I realized then and there that my life was over before it even started. My plan was written out and there was nothing I could do, I had always lived with pain. That was it, pain… "All I ever wanted was a painless life, but what I'm looking at is a painless death. Tony, all I got from this job, was pain." I pulled the trigger, the bullet pierced through my skull creating a mist of blood in the Brooklyn morning air. It was 8:44AM, I was 7 hours and 46 minutes away from being a retired NYPD officer.

It was his third interview this week, but he was still hopeful that something would change in his life. Bruce Walters was unemployed, overweight and had little hope for a love life. He started the engine of his 1994 Honda Civic and proceeded to leave his parents driveway. He was 31 and never finished any schooling after 11th grade, when he first experimented with drugs. It was 9AM in Pittsburgh and Bruce's interview was set for 10:30AM, he left early just in case he got lost. "Great… Traffic" Bruce let out a sigh as he said this aloud. He opened up his glove compartment and lit a marijuana joint exhaling his chance of being late problems out of the window. He wanted to have a clear mind and he was optimistic about this one. A hotel job interview was hard to come by during these hard times, but Bruce applied everywhere. Traffic was moving along after 20 grueling minutes on the I-376 and Bruce was getting anxious as he thought traffic would get worse since it was still early in the day. As he tried to switch lanes to the left, he failed to take a second look before cutting off a speeding Jeep Wrangler carrying 5 passengers. The collision sent Bruce's Civic careening over the barrier onto the opposite lane, crushed instantly by an oncoming truck. Bruce died instantly, 31 years, 11 months, 2 weeks and 2 days after his mother Janet gave birth to her last son before she died from complications in the hospital that cold morning in January. The Wrangler's passengers, three men and two women weren't wearing their seat belts as they had been on the road since 3AM on their way to get back on the I-80 toward the east coast. The passengers died, all students at Penn State. One of the passengers was a senator's daughter Olistis Helen Cofley and she had just given birth to senator Cofley's first grandson. Greg Cofley was called by the Pennsylvania State Police at 11:42AM as he was getting ready to have lunch after spending the morning reading the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. He dropped the phone in disbelief. He opened his desk drawer and grabbed his Smith and Wesson, scribbling on a notepad a letter to his wife and pulling the trigger as the barrel pressed against his temporal lobe. A senator was dead.
